claim: Mean movement during the first active 12 h after the first cage change is negatively associated with later CombZ.
population: All animals with a resolvable first-night window and a CombZ endpoint (n=111)
temporal_scope: First Active phase block after first cage change; fixed clock window 18:30-06:30, 12 h
model: Spearman rank correlation with bootstrap CI
res_sus_outcome_derived: yes - Group is endpoint-derived from CombZ and is excluded from all canonical primary models
remaining_caveat: Association, not causation. CombZ is a downstream composite; RES/SUS labels derive from it.
notes: Stage 16 validation check canonical_feature_registry PASS: exactly three canonical features in required order.

claim: Movement RMSSD over the same window is negatively associated with later CombZ.
temporal_scope: First active 12 h after first cage change
model: Spearman rank correlation with bootstrap CI
remaining_caveat: Supporting association only; not demonstrated as an independent predictive contributor.
notes: Must not be described as an independent predictor.

claim: Entropy persistence (ACF1) over the same window is associated with later CombZ.
temporal_scope: First active 12 h after first cage change
model: Spearman rank correlation with bootstrap CI
current_status: NOT BH-supported; bootstrap CI includes zero
remaining_caveat: Must be reported with the qualified wording. Any claim that Entropy_acf1 is significant is false.
publication_ready: yes as a qualified negative/inconclusive result; NOT as a positive finding
notes: Stage 16 validation check entropy_wording PASS enforces the required qualified wording.

claim: A fixed a priori behaviour-only model using mean movement predicts later CombZ out of sample.
temporal_scope: First active 12 h after first cage change
sensitivity_resolution: UNRESOLVED - Stage 16 records resolution sensitivity as unavailable for canonical export; the legacy 5-min output is deliberately not promoted
model: Fixed a priori behaviour-only model registry; LOAO and repeated grouped 5-fold CV
effect_size: LOAO out-of-sample R2 = 0.1593946 vs training-fold mean; repeated 5-fold CV mean R2 = 0.1558227 [0.1159, 0.1790]; permutation p = 1/1001
res_sus_outcome_derived: yes - Group excluded from the model
remaining_caveat: Internal validation only, not external validation. Prospective association/prediction, not causal inference.
notes: Stage 16 checks movement_mean_headline PASS, permutation_display PASS (exact 1/1001 retained), group_excluded_primary_prediction PASS.

claim: The fixed three-feature behaviour-only model predicts later CombZ out of sample.
temporal_scope: First active 12 h after first cage change
model: Fixed a priori model: Movement_mean + Movement_rmssd + Entropy_acf1
effect_size: LOAO out-of-sample R2 = 0.1524453; repeated 5-fold CV mean R2 = 0.1479031 [0.1028, 0.1800]; permutation p = 1/1001
current_status: Permutation-supported but does NOT improve on Movement_mean alone (0.1524 vs 0.1594)
remaining_caveat: No model-comparison significance test was performed. Must not be described as an improvement over the movement-only model.
notes: Sex-adjusted variants exist as sensitivities (R2 0.1524 and 0.1423) with no permutation test specified.

claim: The three canonical feature-CombZ associations do not differ by sex.
temporal_scope: First active 12 h after first cage change
multiplicity_family: Three canonical primary feature-by-Sex interaction tests (BH)
current_status: No evidence that any association differed by sex
remaining_caveat: Absence of evidence, not evidence of absence; the study is not powered for interaction. Sex-stratified estimates are descriptive and are NOT interaction tests.

claim: Raw movement differs by group across cage changes and light/dark phase.
population: 1221 animal-level movement observations across cage change x phase cells
temporal_scope: Full longitudinal record, CC1-CC4, Active and Inactive phases
model: Pairwise Wilcoxon (Holm within panel); secondary one-way LM; repeated-measures LMM
contrast_or_endpoint: CON/RES/SUS pairwise within each cage change x phase cell
multiplicity_family: Holm within each prespecified three-contrast panel; no global family exported (export_global_family_corrections = FALSE)
effect_size: 214 supplementary result rows: 66 pairwise Wilcoxon, 66 group summaries, 40 descriptive movement-CombZ associations, 22 one-way LM, 14 repeated-measures LMM, 6 sex-stratified
res_sus_outcome_derived: yes - groups are endpoint-derived, so this is phenotype characterization and not independent validation
current_status: Canonical and exported; secondary phenotype/group characterization
remaining_caveat: Descriptive. Does not replace the Stage 09 prospective analysis. No wider global family-wise correction is claimed.

claim: Multiscale behavioural domains during the first night after the first cage change differ by group within sex.
population: n=111 animals; 50 with a complete 72-slot window
temporal_scope: First Active phase block after first cage change; fixed clock window 18:30-06:30, 12 h; expected 72 slots
primary_resolution: 10min (chosen to match canonical Stage 09, which owns the first-12-h question)
sensitivity_resolution: 5min (produced by the same driver; Stage 14 global backbone stays 5min)
model: DomainScore ~ Group * Sex (stats::lm + emmeans), t-based 95pct CI on residual df
contrast_or_endpoint: RES-CON, SUS-CON, SUS-RES within Sex, across 5 displayed domains
multiplicity_family: BH with explicitly declared n: FIRST_NIGHT__Female/Male__DISPLAYED_5x3 (n=15 each); interaction family DISPLAYED_5 (n=5); transparency sensitivity ALL_RAW_8x3 (n=24 each)
effect_size: 1 of 30 displayed cells FDR-supported: Female RES-CON, Behavioral volatility / fragmentation, Hedges g = -1.0093, raw p = 0.001341, q = 0.020108
remaining_caveat: Only 50 of 111 animals have a complete window. Single surviving cell; do not over-read the panel as a multi-domain signature.
publication_ready: yes as a characterization panel, reported with the single FDR-supported cell stated as such
notes: Five displayed domains: volatility/fragmentation, flexibility/predictability, social spatial organization, active-phase adaptation/exploration, psychomotor activation. Three additional raw candidates are audit-only and never displayed. Phase rule is exact membership, not substring matching.

claim: Active-phase latent-state persistence is reduced in SUS relative to CON across the longitudinal record.
temporal_scope: Longitudinal, Active phase, gap-aware sequence segmentation
model: Mixed model with animal random effect; animal-level Hedges g reported alongside
contrast_or_endpoint: SUS-CON and SUS-RES on mean_dwell_minutes, self_transition_probability, state_switch_rate, transition_entropy
multiplicity_family: Not a declared BH family; robustness assessed by sign stability across 5 distinct gap-aware optima
effect_size: SUS-CON sign-stable across all 5 optima: mean_dwell 0.617-0.687 (5/5 nominally sig), self_transition 0.464-0.558 (4/5), state_switch -0.558 to -0.464 (4/5), transition_entropy -0.654 to -0.559 (5/5)
current_status: Cross-optimum robust for the SUS-CON active persistence family
remaining_caveat: Conditional on stating the HMM identifiability caveats. logLik spans 69078-414114 across seeds at 5min, i.e. multiple distinct local optima; several emission SDs sit at the 0.05 floor. Persistence metrics are mutually algebraically related, so these are not four independent findings.
publication_ready: conditional - only with the identifiability caveat stated

claim: Inactive-phase latent-state architecture differs by group (rest/quiescence interpretation).
contrast_or_endpoint: RES-CON and SUS-CON on the inactive persistence family
multiplicity_family: Not declared; sign stability assessed across 5 optima
effect_size: All 10 inactive contrasts are sign-stable and nominally significant across all 5 optima (e.g. mean_dwell SUS-CON -1.092 to -0.979)
current_status: NOT PROMOTED pending measurement validity - statistically robust but not interpretable as biology
remaining_caveat: Inactive-phase observed_fraction is confounded with genuine rest: median 0.149 vs 1.000 in Active, 95.7pct of inactive epochs below 0.50, and inactive domains correlate with mean movement at Spearman rho 0.64-0.87. hard_dropout_signature cannot distinguish chip loss from rest. The phase-aware inactive-QC redesign is SPECIFIED, NOT IMPLEMENTED; chip_loss_qc_mode remains annotate_only.
notes: DECISION REQUIRED: whether to implement the proposed A/B/C relative-read-density classification in production before submission.

claim: Spatial/state occupancy entropy distinguishes groups (occupancy architecture phenotype).
effect_size: Estimate ranges -0.281 to +0.265 across 5 optima; all_same_sign = FALSE; 0 of 5 nominally significant
current_status: EXCLUDED - the audit verdict is literally: NOT robust: sign flips across optima; do not report as a finding
remaining_caveat: Any claim that occupancy architecture is a stable finding is unsupported. Note the Active SUS-CON occupancy_entropy contrast IS sign-stable but is not nominally significant at any optimum.

claim: First-night latent-state dwell time differs by group.
population: 109 animals with a first-night dwell value
temporal_scope: First active 12 h after first cage change
model: HMM dwell extracted from the shipped fit, compared against a seed-7 refit
contrast_or_endpoint: Animal-level dwell agreement; RES-CON/SUS-CON/SUS-RES within Sex
effect_size: Shipped vs refit Spearman rho = 0.0154; mean dwell 32.06 vs 16.51 min (1.94x). Contrast estimates and nominal p-values are not stable across seeds.
current_status: EXCLUDED - animal-level first-night dwell is essentially uncorrelated between fits
remaining_caveat: Any claim that first-night HMM persistence is robust is unsupported. A 12 h window is too short to identify the state model stably. This is distinct from the longitudinal active persistence family, which IS cross-optimum stable.
notes: This is the single clearest instability in the repository and the strongest reason not to build a first-night latent-state claim.

claim: Behavioural latent axes are associated with proteomic module scores.
population: Male neuron/neuropil subset only; n per model ranges 0-9
temporal_scope: Behavioural features aggregated to animal level; proteomics at terminal timepoint
model: Spearman correlation between behavioural and proteomic latent axes
multiplicity_family: BH within the curated model set (spearman_fdr)
effect_size: 0 of 40 models reach FDR < 0.05; all 40 are labelled ClaimType=associative, EvidenceUse=exploratory_effect_size_small_n, StableForMainText=FALSE
current_status: EXPLORATORY - no result is main-text stable; n is too small
remaining_caveat: n = 0-9 per model. The script itself marks every model StableForMainText = FALSE. Keep separate from the behavioural source-data workbook.
notes: Stage 15 was migrated to the canonical Stage 09 10-min source and canonical identity, with an explicit validated ID crosswalk.
